title: Food chains and ecosystems
intro: Who eats whom? Learn about producers and consumers, food chains and webs, photosynthesis and how living things depend on each other.
description: Free KS3 Biology questions with answers on ecosystems: food chains and food webs, producers, consumers, predators and prey, photosynthesis, adaptation and decomposers. Marked instantly, for Year 7, 8 and 9.

questions.q: In the food chain grass → rabbit → fox, what is the grass?
questions.explain: Grass is a producer: it makes its own food by photosynthesis. Every food chain starts with a producer.

questions.q: In a food chain, what do the arrows show?
options: The direction energy moves, from the eaten to the eater
questions.hint: The arrow points to the animal doing the eating.
questions.explain: The arrows show energy passing from the food to the animal that eats it.

questions.q: An animal that eats only plants is called…
questions.hint: Herb- is to do with plants.
questions.explain: Herbivores eat plants. Carnivores eat other animals. Omnivores eat both.

questions.q: In grass → rabbit → fox, which animal is the **predator**?
questions.hint: A predator hunts and eats other animals.
questions.explain: The fox is the predator and the rabbit is its prey.

questions.q: In a food web, foxes eat rabbits. A disease kills most of the foxes. What will probably happen to the rabbits at first?
questions.explain: With fewer foxes eating them, more rabbits survive, so the rabbit population goes up (at least at first).

questions.q: What do **decomposers** such as fungi and bacteria do?
options: Break down dead things and return nutrients to the soil
questions.explain: Decomposers break down dead plants and animals, putting nutrients back into the soil for plants to use.

questions.q: Plants make their own food by…
questions.explain: Plants use light energy to make glucose. This is photosynthesis.

questions.hint: Plants take in carbon dioxide and water, and give out oxygen.
questions.explain: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen, using light energy absorbed by chlorophyll.

questions.q: Which gas do plants give out during photosynthesis?
questions.hint: It's the gas we breathe in.
questions.explain: Plants give out oxygen. Almost all the oxygen in the air was made by photosynthesis.

questions.q: Where does a plant get the **water** for photosynthesis?
options: From the soil, through its roots
From the air, through its leaves
questions.explain: Water is absorbed from the soil by the roots (especially root hair cells) and travels up to the leaves.

questions.q: A polar bear has thick fur and a layer of fat. What are these?
options: Adaptations to keep it warm in the cold
Ways to catch food in the desert
questions.hint: Polar bears live in the Arctic.
questions.explain: Features that help a living thing survive where it lives are adaptations. Fur and fat insulate the bear.

questions.q: A cactus has spines instead of leaves. How does this help it survive in a desert?
questions.hint: Water is scarce in the desert.
questions.explain: Spines have a tiny surface area, so the cactus loses less water. They also stop animals eating it.

questions.q: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower. How does this help plants?
options: It pollinates them so they can make seeds
It makes the plants grow taller
It protects the plants from frost
questions.hint: Pollen needs to reach another flower.
questions.explain: Bees pollinate flowers, so the plants can make seeds. That's why a fall in bee numbers worries farmers.

questions.q: Living things in an area all depend on each other. This is called…
questions.explain: Interdependence means living things rely on each other for food, shelter, pollination and more. A change to one can affect many others.
